newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- cash softer, deals loom.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- cash softer, deals loom.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bonds were quoted down as much as 3/8 of a point by midday as players looked into the jaws of a $7 billion new issue week.
The $7 billion includes a $2.7 billion taxable New Jersey Economic Development Authority deal via Merrill Lynch & Co.
Traders pegged prices anywhere from unchanged to down 3/8 of point, but all agreed the calendar was one to be reckoned with.

"A lot of deals are going to be priced here, and you have the tight ratios in munis," one trader said, adding that long municipals have been yielding roughly 80 percent of U.S. Treasury bonds. "So they are probably going to back off a little with all the new issue supply coming."

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 1/32 at 99-15/32 to yield 6.67 percent. In debt futures, the September municipal contract was down 21/32 at 117-22/32. The September T-bond contract was down 5/32 at 112-12/32. The MOB spread was 170 ticks.
One trader linked the muni contract's sharp drop to actions leading up to last week's June contract settlement.

The trader said some players were running up index bonds last week and the week before in order to enhance the value of the contract, which on expiration is cash settled at the price of the Bond Buyer's 40-Bond Index.
"And now, Index bonds, nobody wants them, nobody cares," the trader said. "Positions have all been liquidated, the money is in the pocket, that's what's going on."
Players who had long positions in muni contracts or options bid up index bonds, and in doing so drove up the broader muni market, he said.
Now, "they pulled their bids, and now those bonds have to go to what they are worth in the marketplace," he said.

As for the week's calendar, negotiated offerings are expected to total $5.7 billion in 60 sales, including the $2.7 billion New Jersey Economic Development Authority deal. Merrill is expected to begin a retail order period on the issue on Monday.
Late Friday, the state said it had secured bids from insurers for the entire deal.
On the competitive side, 70 sales totaling $1.3 billion are scheduled for the week. A $300 million Massachusettes deal on Tuesday is the largest.
